name: Oblivion Ring
oracle_text:
When this enchantment enters, exile another target nonland permanent.
When this enchantment leaves the battlefield, return the exiled card to the battlefield under its owner's control.
blocked_sentences: When this enchantment leaves the battlefield, return the exiled card to the battlefield under its owner's control.

needs.what: a persistent link recorded on the exiling permanent (or on the exiled object) naming which cards it exiled, written by `exile` and readable by a later, separate ability resolution of the same permanent - the O-Ring / Banishing Light / Fiend Hunter family all need exactly this one link
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `snapshot` is the documented answer to last-known information, but it writes into `EffectContext.bindings`, which lives only for one resolution: the `self_enters` trigger and the `leaves_battlefield` trigger are two separate abilities with two separate contexts, so a snapshot taken by the first is gone before the second runs. `exile` itself takes only `objects` and stores nothing about who exiled what (`zones.exile` just calls `move_object` with `cause="exiled"`), so after the enchantment leaves there is nothing anywhere that says which card in exile was its victim.

needs.what: a selector key that names the cards exiled by the source permanent, e.g. `{"zone": "exile", "exiled_with": "self"}`, resolvable from a `leaves_battlefield` trigger after the source has already left the battlefield
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `SELECTOR_KEYS` has no exile-linkage key. `{"target": "t1"}` only reaches targets chosen for the ability currently resolving, and `{"binding": ...}` only reaches that resolution's bindings - the leaves trigger binds `subject`, `self` and `was_attacking`, none of which is the exiled card. The only selector that reaches exile at all is a plain `{"zone": "exile", ...}` filter, which matches every card in exile from every source, so `put_onto_battlefield` over it would return cards this enchantment never exiled. That is a different card, not an approximation of this one.

needs.what: `leaves_battlefield` with `source: "self"` needs to carry the source's exile link into the trigger's bindings at the moment the permanent leaves, the way `was_attacking` is snapshotted for an object that has already gone
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `leaves_battlefield` fires correctly with `source: "self"`, but its bindings are built fresh per trigger and carry no memory of what the permanent did while it was on the battlefield. `delay` is the one op whose bindings are captured early, and its `step` vocabulary is `upkeep`/`draw_step`/`begin_combat`/`end_step` - turn-based moments, not "when this permanent leaves" - so it cannot schedule the return either.
